dioscorides.excerpt: θύμος· γινώσκεται ὑπὸ πάντων. θαμνίσκιον φρυγανοειδές, φυλλαρίοις στενοῖς καὶ πολλοῖς περιειλημμένον, ἔχον ἐπ᾿ ἄκρου κεφάλια ἄνθους ⟨περίπλεα⟩, πορφυρίζοντα.
dioscorides.edition: Wellmann 1906, Pedanii Dioscuridis Anazarbei De materia medica vol. II (libri III-IV), Berlin: Weidmann; read from page scan on archive.org (BIUSante_65865x02), p. 48 (⟨περίπλεα⟩ is Wellmann's supplement)

identification.source: Sprengel 1830, vol. 2, pp. 511-512 (Comm. III cap. XXXVIII): 'Thymum Dioscoridis legitimum, quem Brunfelsius, Tragus ac Fuchsius pro Thymo vulgari habuerant, Matthiolus primus in Thymo cretico Brot. (Satureia capitata L.) recognovisse videtur'; describes the plant, abundant on Hymettus. Satureia capitata L. is the basionym-era name of Thymbra capitata. 'probable' because Sprengel records the earlier rival identification (Thymus vulgaris) and says 'videtur'. | Fraas 1845, p. 174: 'Sat. capitata L., Satureystrauch' = θύμος Hippocr., λευκὸς θύμος Theophr. 6,1,2, θύμος Diosc. 3,38; modern θυμάρι 'frequentiss. appellatio'; very common scrub on dry plains, hills and foothills to 2500 ft throughout. Osbaldeston 2000, ch. 3-44 THUMOS: SUGGESTED Thymus angustifolius, Thymus glaber (Wild Thyme) - a competing candidate. (https://archive.org/details/BIUSante_dioscsprengelx02/page/n512/mode/1up ; https://archive.org/details/synopsisplantaru00fraa/page/n219/mode/1up)

alternatives.name: Thymus vulgaris L.
alternatives.source: Brunfels, Tragus, Fuchs, cited (superseded) by Sprengel 1830, vol. 2, p. 511

caveats: Identification is probable; results describe Thymbra capitata (L.) Cav., which may not be the plant Dioscorides meant.
